subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Large Hadron Collider: World's Biggest Machine
description: A fast breakdown of The Large Hadron Collider: World's Biggest Machine for builders.

hook.text: The Large Hadron Collider is a 17-mile ring buried 300 feet under the Swiss-French border. It recreates post-Big Bang conditions.

buildup.text: Protons travel at 99.9999991% light speed inside the ring. Superconducting magnets cooled to -456 degrees F bend their path.

discovery.text: Magnets must be aligned within a fraction of a millimeter over 17 miles. Even Earth's tidal forces distort the tunnel measurably.

twist.text: In 2008, a faulty solder joint caused a helium explosion that damaged 53 magnets. Repairs took 14 months before first collisions.

climax.text: The LHC confirmed the Higgs boson in 2012 — a particle predicted 48 years earlier. Engineering made theoretical physics real.

punchline.text: 17 miles. Near absolute zero. Near light speed. One particle found.

quiz.question: What initial setback delayed the LHC's first particle collisions?
options: The tunnel flooded after an underground aquifer was accidentally breached
A faulty solder joint caused a helium explosion that damaged 53 magnets
The superconducting magnets couldn't maintain the required temperature
